newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Pojistovna shrs overvalued -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech Pojistovna shrs overvalued -analysts.

text.p: Shares in the largest Czech insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s. are overvalued and uncertainties surrounding the company's future should encourage investors to sell soon, analysts say.

On Monday, Pojistovna lost 41 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) to 3,450 putting the issue eight percent below its price of one month ago - almost the same decline as suffered by the PX50 as a whole over the same period.

However, analysts believe the stock is still overvalued and say that their concerns rest on three factors, including how the insurer's new main shareholder, investment group PPF, affects the running of the company.

Also much depends of whether Pojistovna can sustain its dominant position on the domestic insurance market, and how the failures of part-owned subsidiary banks - Kreditni Banka Plzen a.s. and Pragobanka a.s. - affect the company's financial position this year and next.
Ceska Pojistivna has, analysts say, little problem raising money through insurance but is less adept at putting it to good use on the capital markets.
"Pojistovna's strength has always been in insuring and not in investing money," said one local analyst who declined to be named.
Pojistovna's most spectacular losses came with the failure of Kreditini Banka Plzen, of which it is a majority owner.
Kreditni was taken into forced administration by the Czech National Bank earlier this year with losses estimated at around four billion crowns.
The fall of Pragobnka, which lost 800 million crowns in 1995, added further to the insurer's financial woes.
All the analysts polled by Reuters said the current share price of 3,450 was too high and refused to recommend buying into the company at anything over 3,000 crowns per share.
They also said the share price reflected uncertainty about the stability of the current ownership structure of the insurer.
"The (share) price is probably a reflection of anticipated shifts in the ownership structure," said Leos Jirman, an analyst at BH Securities.
The Czech government's main privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, holds 26 percent of Pojistovna but no timetable for selling off the stake has been agreed.
In order to cover some of the losses from Kreditni and Pragobanka, Ceska Pojistovna is pushing through a rights issue valued at over four billion crowns.

In the course of the rights issue, IPB Bank says it wants to transfer its share to PPF which would then become Pojistovna's biggest shareholder (36 percent) at the same time as owning an option to buy a further 14 percent currently held by Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.
In September, Ceska Pojistovna said it did not expect to post a profit in 1996 and could post a loss after net profits of 413 million crowns last year.
The insurer reported on Monday a gross profit of 85.2 million crowns for the first nine months of 1996. No comparatives were given.
